chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Abu al-Abbas al-Baqqaq, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man maraws a slave-girl without the permission of her owners.
He (peace be upon him) said: "It is fornication (Zina), for indeed Allah, the Exalted, says: 'Marry them with the permission of their owners.'"
As for that which indicates that the children will be slaves, what he narrated is:
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying a slave girl without her owner's permission?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that marrying a female slave without her owner's consent is classified as Zina, explicitly linking this ruling to the Quranic command to marry them 'with the permission of their owners.' This narration, found in Tahdhib al-Ahkam, underscores the contractual nature of concubinage in Shia jurisprudence and establishes the principle of 'Umm al-Walad,' where the child inherits the mother's status of slavery.
